questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on his glans penis for 2 weeks. Examination reveals a solitary, indurated, non-tender ulcer with a clean base. Inguinal lymphadenopathy is firm and non-tender. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents as a painless, indurated chancre with non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Chancroid is painful; herpes is painful with vesicles; LGV causes tender lymphadenopathy.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a verrucous plaque on his foot with sinus tracts discharging black granules. Which of the following organisms is most commonly responsible?
questions.exp: Madura foot (eumycetoma) with black granules is most commonly caused by Madurella mycetomatis, a true fungus. White/yellow granules suggest actinomycetoma (bacterial).

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on the trunk and extremities. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposition at the dermo-epidermal junction. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid shows linear IgG and C3 along the BMZ (against BP180/BP230). Pemphigus shows intercellular IgG (fish-net pattern). DH shows granular IgA; Linear IgA shows linear IgA.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with hypopigmented macules, loss of sensation over the lesions, and thickened greater auricular nerve. Slit skin smear is negative. Histopathology shows epithelioid cell granulomas with Langhans giant cells. The type of leprosy is:
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) features: few hypopigmented anesthetic macules, thickened nerves, AFB-negative SSS, and well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans cells on histopathology.

questions.q: A patient on dapsone therapy for leprosy develops sudden-onset pallor, jaundice, and dark urine on the 4th week of treatment. Blood smear shows Heinz bodies. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent hemolytic anemia, especially in G6PD-deficient patients. Heinz bodies indicate oxidative hemolysis. Dapsone should be stopped and clofazimine substituted as the third drug in PB/MB regimens.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive patient develops grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along a single dermatome on the left chest wall. The agent causing this condition has the ability to remain latent in:
questions.exp: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) causing herpes zoster remains latent in the posterior (dorsal) root ganglia and trigeminal ganglia. Reactivation occurs due to immunosuppression.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child presents with honey-crusted lesions around the mouth and nose. Gram stain of the exudate shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. First-line treatment for non-bullous impetigo without systemic symptoms is:
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo caused by Staph aureus or Strep pyogenes is first treated with topical mupirocin or retapamulin. Systemic antibiotics are reserved for extensive disease or systemic symptoms.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman with known SLE presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers. ANA is positive with anti-dsDNA antibodies. Which complement pathway is primarily activated in lupus nephritis?
questions.exp: In lupus nephritis, immune complex deposition activates the classical complement pathway (C1q binding to IgG/IgM). This leads to consumption of C3 and C4, causing low serum complement levels.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with well-defined erythematous plaques with silvery scales on his elbows and scalp. He reports joint pain in his distal interphalangeal joints. The nail changes most specific to this condition are:
questions.exp: Nail pitting (thimble pitting) and onycholysis are characteristic of psoriasis. Oil drop sign (salmon patch) is also specific. Pitting results from psoriatic involvement of the proximal nail matrix.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with annular erythematous lesions with central clearing and a scaly border on her trunk. KOH mount shows septate hyphae. The drug of choice for widespread tinea corporis is:
questions.exp: For widespread or resistant dermatophytosis, oral antifungals are preferred. Itraconazole (200 mg/day for 1-2 weeks) and terbinafine (250 mg/day for 2-4 weeks) are most effective. Griseofulvin is less preferred due to longer duration and resistance.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with painful genital ulcers associated with tender inguinal lymphadenopathy that becomes fluctuant (buboes). Gram stain shows 'school of fish' arrangement of Gram-negative bacilli. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi, showing 'school of fish' or 'rail road track' pattern on Gram stain. It presents with painful soft ulcers and tender inguinal buboes.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, telangiectasias, and dysphagia. Anti-centromere antibodies are positive. This presentation is consistent with:
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (limited systemic sclerosis) includes Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, and Telangiectasias. Anti-centromere antibodies are highly specific for CREST.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a pearly nodule with rolled edges and central ulceration on his nose. He has a history of prolonged sun exposure. The most common type of skin cancer in humans is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer in humans (accounts for ~75-80% of all skin cancers). It typically presents as a pearly nodule with telangiectasias and rolled/pearly borders on sun-exposed areas.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with multiple satellite lesions around the diaper area with pustules and a beefy-red base. KOH mount is positive. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Candidal diaper dermatitis presents with satellite lesions, pustules, and beefy erythema. Topical nystatin (or miconazole/clotrimazole) is first-line treatment. Hydrocortisone alone is contraindicated as it worsens candidiasis.

questions.q: A patient presents with a Type 1 lepra reaction after starting MDT. Features include painful erythematous lesions in existing patches with neuritis. The treatment of choice for this reaction is:
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction is a delayed hypersensitivity reaction requiring oral prednisolone (40-60 mg/day tapered over 3-6 months). Thalidomide is used for ENL (Type 2 reaction). MDT should NOT be stopped.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with periorbital heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules over knuckles, and proximal muscle weakness. CPK is elevated. The most common internal malignancy associated with this condition in adults is:
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis in adults (especially women >40 years) is associated with ovarian carcinoma most commonly, followed by lung and breast cancer. A thorough malignancy workup is mandatory in adult-onset dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 20-year-old man presents with multiple grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the sacrum. The lesions recur every month. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. The antiviral of choice for suppressive therapy is:
questions.exp: Recurrent genital herpes (HSV-2) is managed with daily suppressive therapy using acyclovir 400 mg twice daily. This reduces frequency of recurrences by 70-80% and reduces viral shedding.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with symmetrical pruritic papulovesicles on extensor surfaces of elbows and knees. Direct immunofluorescence shows granular IgA deposits at dermal papilla. She also has villous atrophy on intestinal biopsy. Diagnosis and treatment?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis shows granular IgA at dermal papilla tips and is associated with celiac disease. Treatment is dapsone for rapid symptom relief and strict gluten-free diet for long-term remission.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a pigmented lesion with an irregular border, variegated color (black, brown, red), and diameter >6mm. Dermoscopy shows atypical pigment network. The staging system used for melanoma is based on:
opts: Both Clark's level and Breslow's thickness
questions.exp: Current AJCC staging of melanoma primarily uses Breslow's thickness (depth of invasion in mm) as the most important prognostic factor. Clark's levels are no longer used in AJCC 8th edition staging.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with flexural lichenified plaques with intense pruritus since childhood. She also has asthma and allergic rhinitis. Serum IgE is markedly elevated. The defective structural protein in the epidermal barrier in this condition is:
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis involves loss-of-function mutations in filaggrin (FLG gene), a key structural protein that maintains the epidermal barrier. Filaggrin deficiency leads to barrier dysfunction and sensitization to allergens.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with painful nodules over the shins, fever, and joint pains. He has a history of sore throat 2 weeks ago. The most common causative factor is:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum is most commonly caused by Streptococcal pharyngitis (preceding streptococcal infection) in most studies. Other causes include TB, sarcoidosis, drugs (OCP), IBD, and fungal infections.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with flaccid blisters that rupture to form erosions predominantly on the trunk. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposition in a 'fish-net' pattern. The autoantigen in this condition is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris is caused by autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 (and desmoglein 1 in mucocutaneous variant). IIF shows intercellular IgG deposition ('fish-net' or 'chicken wire' pattern).

questions.q: A 2-year-old child presents with verrucous papules on the fingers and plantar surface. The causative HPV types for plantar warts are:
questions.exp: Plantar warts (verruca plantaris) are caused by HPV types 1 (myrmecia) and 2 (mosaic warts). HPV 6 and 11 cause condylomata acuminata; HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk types causing cervical carcinoma.

questions.q: A patient presents with erythema, desquamation, and lymphadenopathy involving >90% of body surface area. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Erythroderma is defined as erythema and scaling involving >90% of the BSA. Common causes include psoriasis, eczema, drug reactions, lymphoma (Sezary syndrome), and pityriasis rubra pilaris.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with woody induration of both legs, non-pitting edema, and lymphorrhea. Lymphoscintigraphy confirms lymphatic obstruction. The skin change of hyperkeratosis with cobblestone appearance is called:
questions.exp: Elephantiasis nostras verrucosa (ENV) is chronic lymphedema with hyperkeratosis, fibrosis, papillomatosis, and cobblestone/mossy verrucous changes due to longstanding lymphatic insufficiency.

questions.q: A 19-year-old man presents with multiple painful genital ulcers. The ulcers are non-indurated with undermined edges. A smear from the base shows Gram-negative coccobacilli arranged in 'school of fish' pattern. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Chancroid (H. ducreyi) is treated with azithromycin 1g single dose or ceftriaxone 250mg IM single dose, or ciprofloxacin 500mg twice daily for 3 days. Azithromycin single dose is preferred for compliance.

questions.q: Patch testing is used to diagnose which type of hypersensitivity reaction?
questions.exp: Patch testing diagnoses allergic contact dermatitis, which is a Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity reaction mediated by sensitized T lymphocytes. Reading is done at 48 and 96 hours.

questions.q: A 26-year-old woman presents with erythematous plaques, photosensitivity, malar rash, and ANA positivity. She recently started hydralazine for hypertension. The most characteristic autoantibody in drug-induced lupus is:
questions.exp: Drug-induced lupus erythematosus (DILE) characteristically shows anti-histone antibodies. Common causing drugs include hydralazine, procainamide, isoniazid, and minocycline. Anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm are specific for idiopathic SLE.

questions.q: A 40-year-old HIV-positive man presents with painless ulcers with 'beefy red' granulomatous base and raised edges on the genitalia. Tissue smear shows macrophages filled with Donovan bodies (safety pin appearance). The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Granuloma inguinale (donovanosis) is caused by Klebsiella granulomatis. Pathognomonic Donovan bodies are intracytoplasmic inclusions seen in macrophages with a closed safety pin appearance on Giemsa stain.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with hyperpigmented macules over the malar region bilaterally after starting oral contraceptives. Wood's lamp examination accentuates the pigmentation. This condition is best described as:
questions.exp: Melasma presents as symmetrical hyperpigmentation on sun-exposed areas, especially malar region. Wood's lamp accentuates epidermal melasma (increased fluorescence), confirming superficial melanin. OCP is a common trigger.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with prurigo nodularis-like lesions, eosinophilia, and peripheral neuropathy. He has lived in a tropical country. Skin snip from the iliac crest shows microfilariae without sheaths. The vector responsible for transmission is:
questions.exp: Onchocerciasis (river blindness) is caused by Onchocerca volvulus, transmitted by Simulium blackfly (blackflies breeding in fast-flowing rivers). Unsheathed microfilariae are seen in skin snips. It causes 'leopard skin', onchodermatitis, and blindness.
